title: A computational clinical decision-supporting system to suggest effective anti-epileptic drugs for pediatric epilepsy patients based on deep learning models using patient's medical history.
summary: The decision-support system reports AUROCs 0.90/0.80/0.92 and hold-out PPVs 0.92/0.97/0.91 for vigabatrin, prednisolone and clobazam.
ai_technology: Three multi-channel CNNs learn from 7,507 records of 1,000 pediatric epilepsy patients to predict effectiveness of three specified AEDs.
organization: Department of Biomedical Engineering, Chung-Ang University, 84 Heukseok-ro, Dongjak-gu, Seoul, Republic of Korea

evidence.tested: The decision-support system reports AUROCs 0.90/0.80/0.92 and hold-out PPVs 0.92/0.97/0.91 for vigabatrin, prednisolone and clobazam.
evidence.unknown: Results are limited to the reported models, cohorts, datasets or experiments; broader generalization and clinical or operational benefit were not established.
